topic: Your client finds out their employee's residency visa expired from the airport — not from you
format: Open with a question that forces the reader to calculate their own answer — time lost, money wasted, or risk carried
post:
An employee stopped at Muscat International. A visa expiry sitting unread in a WhatsApp thread. A phone call to HR at 11pm — and no one had seen it coming.

Most HR managers in Oman can't see it coming either. Not because they're careless, but because the system they're working with isn't really a system at all.

That gap between "I think we're fine" and "we have a problem" tends to close at the worst possible moment — an airport, a border, a client site.

A business owner I spoke with found out his employee's residency visa had expired when the employee was stopped at Muscat International. Not from an alert. Not from a calendar reminder. From a phone call at 11pm.

The scramble that followed cost two days of work, a cancelled client visit, and a fine. The visa expiry had been sitting in a WhatsApp message nobody actioned.

That's what manual work permit tracking actually looks like in Oman. Not a minor slip — a missed renewal that turns into a compliance crisis on someone's worst Tuesday.

Work permit tracking shouldn't live in a chat thread. It needs deadlines, assigned owners, and an audit trail that doesn't depend on someone scrolling back through messages.
